page.layout: One printed page, running text in one column with a narrow margin of notes on the left, cut off at the scan edge. Top: running head centred and page number at top right. Body: running text, then a centred numbered thesis "IX." with title, centred Greek heading "Ἐξήγησις.", then the numbered paragraph "I." Bottom: signature "D 2" and catchword "ginem" at the right.

main_text.p: Vt exigua & minima, contemnimus, indagatio ipsa rerum tum maximarum tum etiam occultissimarum habet oblectationem. Si vero aliquod occurrat, quod verisimile videatur, humanissima completur animus voluptate. Idem 5. Tusc. quaest. Nihil est dulcius otio literato, his dico literis, quibus infinitatem rerum atque naturae, & in hoc ipso mundo, coelum, terras, maria cognoscimus. Eandem in rem videatur Aristoteles l. 1. de partibus animal. cap. 5. Plinius libro 18. cap. 15. Et libro 15. cap. 15. Seneca libro 6. quaest. nat. Sed ante hos longe voluptatem sensit Dauid Regius Propheta, Psalmo 92. cum ait in operibus manuum tuarum ex-ulto.

III. Appellatur igitur hic finis internus, quia ex ipsis scientiae fontibus, & rerum consideratarum natura promanat. Vnde idem Cicero eleganter, Quo-circa intelligi necesse est, in ipsis rebus, quae discuntur & cognoscuntur, invitamenta inesse, quibus ad discendum cognoscendumque moveamur.
main_text.head: Minus principalis & externus est usus multiplex, quem praestat Physica aliis disciplinis, Theologiae, Iurisprudentiae, Medicae, Ethicae.
Ἐξήγησις.
main_text.p: I. Etsi Theologia Physicae limites quam longissime transscendit: ingeniter tamen illam Physica quoque illustrat, cuius lumine penitus haud aspernatur. Quo-ties enim ad naturam nos amandant sacrae literae? quoties naturae thesauros ostentant; & ad inda-

page.notes: The left margin is cut off at the scan edge; only fragments are legible and are not transcribed as notes. Visible fragments include "AR.", "Cato", "cum ea", "naturalia", "Epist. 16", "inquit, cum", and "sibi videret". The left margin also carries further partial lines that cannot be read reliably. Doubtful readings: "5" after "Idem" (printed as a long-s-like glyph), "15" in "libro 15. cap. 15." (printed as a 5-like glyph), "oblectationem" (printed with a ligature), and the page number at top right. The word "exultato" in the printed Psalm reference appears as "ex-vlto" split across a line break. The Greek heading is set in capitals and may need checking against the scan.
